definitions.gloss: dark gray; charcoal gray; deep gray
definitions.explanation: A dark shade of gray approaching black. Used to describe colors in fashion, materials, and natural phenomena. Formed with the prefix 濃 (dark, deep, concentrated) added to 灰色 (gray).

examples.japanese: {濃灰色|のうはいいろ}のスーツが{似合|にあ}う。
examples.english: A dark gray suit looks good on you.

examples.japanese: {雨雲|あまぐも}が{濃灰色|のうはいいろ}に{空|そら}を{覆|おお}っている。
examples.english: Rain clouds are covering the sky in dark gray.

examples.japanese: {車|くるま}の{色|いろ}は{濃灰色|のうはいいろ}を{選|えら}んだ。{汚|よご}れが{目立|めだ}ちにくいからだ。
examples.english: I chose dark gray for the car color because it doesn't show dirt easily.

notes:
Composed of {濃|のう} (dark, deep, concentrated) and {灰色|はいいろ} (gray). Often used in fashion and design contexts. In everyday speech, {濃|こ}い{灰色|はいいろ} (using the i-adjective form) is more common, while {濃灰色|のうはいいろ} appears more in written descriptions, product catalogs, and formal color designations.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {濃灰色|のうはいいろ}の{背景|はいけい}: dark gray background
- {濃灰色|のうはいいろ}の{石|いし}: dark gray stone
- {濃灰色|のうはいいろ}のコート: dark gray coat

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {薄灰色|うすはいいろ}: light gray — the lighter counterpart
- チャコールグレー: charcoal gray — the English loanword, commonly used in fashion
- {鼠色|ねずみいろ}: mouse gray — a traditional Japanese color name for medium gray
